Hester Crane.narrative: I keep the foundry's books, and I know to the crate how short we are on the Lanternquay order. My father is proud and will not admit it, so I write to Mercy Abbot without telling him how far the letters go. Two years ago Tobin Marrow shamed me before both towns, and I have not forgotten; but I was relieved when he broke it, and that is mine to keep.
goals: Meet the Lanternquay stone order without breaking the works
Settle Lanternquay's debt before another load goes down
Reopen northern trade with Brackenford through Mercy Abbot
Keep the foundry books straight and her own counsel
Learn to read a contract as well as she reads a ledger
See the Lanternquay debt settled and the foundry's name clean

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: father
relations.note: I keep his books and his secrets, but I cannot tell him how far my letters go.

relations.name: Prudence Crane
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She feeds the Council and hears everything; I can be quiet with her.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: former betrothed
relations.note: He shamed me before both towns; I will not forget, though I was glad of it.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: correspondent
relations.note: She wants the gate-due gone and trade back; I write to her without my father knowing how far.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: clerk
relations.note: He wrote the seawall indenture; I copied it and know the clause is ambiguous.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: She carries our stone south and wants the debt settled; we are polite.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: She has not paid for the last load and calls our price a drowning man's price.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: His fear keeps the ridge closed and the order short; I wish he would answer for it.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: workman
relations.note: He works cheap and well; my father uses him, and I count his hours in the book.

relations.name: Bisi Oyelaran
relations.label: would-be apprentice
relations.note: She wants to learn the foundry books from me; she is quick and I am inclined to teach her.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He brings our stone north and pays the gate-due. He hates it and I do not blame him.

relations.name: Ambrose Vell
relations.label: council master
relations.note: He says little at the Council table and means all of it. He grumbles at the gate-due as I do, and he has never once asked me to soften a figure in the book.

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: quarry tally-keeper
relations.note: Her tally is the cleanest of any crew's, and she says to my face that her husband was careless on the ridge. I would rather have her honesty than his excuses.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He builds the seawall crates and complains about Dele's wages in the same breath. He is owed for brick and he is owed nothing for the grudge.

relations.name: Ife Oyelaran
relations.label: terrace cook
relations.note: She feeds the terrace's children for a mark a bowl and says the works' kitchen could pay more. She is not wrong, and I write the figures that prove it.

relations.name: Lottie Fenwick
relations.label: stallkeeper's daughter
relations.note: She has a good eye for a cracked pot and a better one for people. She stays friendly with Bisi though her father will not, and I notice such things.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: ironware trader
relations.note: She trades our foundry's seconds and never tries to hide a flaw in them. Her stall fee is owed and she will get it; I keep the book straight.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: works cook
relations.note: She wants Silas off the road and I want the stone moving. We have argued it over the kitchen table and neither of us has won.

relations.name: Wenna Marrow
relations.label: the other woman
relations.note: The town blames her and my mother blames her, but she did not break the promise. I cannot look at her without seeing the broken match, and that is my burden, not hers.

relations.name: Wick Quell
relations.label: fisher
relations.note: He fishes his uncle's drowned boat and resents our stone price. His mother owes us for the last load; he will hear the tally from me sooner or later.

memories.gist: Tobin broke our match a month before the wedding and married Wenna; I stood in the foundry yard while the town talked.
I was relieved when it ended; I did not want to leave the works for Brackenford.
I copied the seawall indenture into the foundry book and saw the clause could be read two ways.
I began writing to Mercy Abbot about reopening the northern trade, without telling my father how far it goes.
My mother set the Council's table after a sitting and I heard the masters argue the tithe and the stone price.

stances.why: The numbers are the only thing in the works that cannot be argued with.
They owe us for the last load, and we cannot carry them forever.
The ridge is closed and the order is short; Brackenford is the way to cover it.
My father would rather buy time than break his word, and I will not shame him.
Tobin shamed me before both towns; I will not forget, even if I was glad.

Hester Crane.secret: I was relieved when Tobin broke the match; I did not want to leave the works.
pastimes: Walking the kiln yard at dusk to check the fires before the night shift
Reading old ledgers and contracts for the pleasure of catching a bad figure
Sitting by the clock tower with a cup of tea, listening to it strike
Hester Crane.calling: I keep the foundry's books, and I would keep them better than any clerk in Kettlebridge if my father would only let me near the contracts as well as the columns.

Josiah Crane.narrative: I am foundry master and chair of the Works Council, and I built this works with my hands and my word. Aldric Marrow's son insulted my house when he broke his promise to Hester, and Kettlebridge remembers: stone goes south now as much as north. The cairn cutting closed the ridge, and I will not beg a giant's pardon, but the Lanternquay order must be met.
goals: Meet the Lanternquay seawall order and keep the works' name
Reopen the ridge quarry without begging the giants
Get Pell back and make an example of him
Keep the gate-due fought at every turn
Master a new casting for the seawall blocks that no other works on the island can match
See the ridge quarry open again and the cairn business put behind Kettlebridge

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She keeps my books and knows the works better than any clerk; I am proud of her.

relations.name: Prudence Crane
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps my house and my table, and the Council eats from her hand.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His son insulted my house, and he keeps the gate-due that robs every carter.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: betrayer
relations.note: He broke his promise to my daughter and shamed my house before both towns.

relations.name: Ambrose Vell
relations.label: council second
relations.note: Slow to speak and slower to forgive; he sits with me and I count on him.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: clerk
relations.note: He holds the contracts and reads the seawall clause against me; I want it read again.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: He led the cutting and now will not climb; his fear costs the works, and he must answer.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He has been robbed twice and still carries our stone; I trust him on the road.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: hired hand
relations.note: He works cheap and does not complain; the quay folk are useful.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He builds the seawall crates and resents the cheap hands; I keep him working.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: She has not paid for the last load and calls our price a drowning man's price.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: runaway apprentice
relations.note: He ran from his indenture; I hold it and want him back to answer for it.

relations.name: Silas Vance
relations.label: foreman
relations.note: He worked the cutting beside Ezra and has not gone back up. He is steadier than Ezra, and I need him.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: She carries our stone south and reads the clause her way. She will have her marks when the stone is cut.

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: quarry tally
relations.note: She keeps the quarry tally straight and tells me her husband was careless. I would hear that from her before I hear it from anyone.

relations.name: Corwin Vance
relations.label: quarry hand
relations.note: Silas's boy works the floor and wants his father's place. Ambition is no bad thing in a quarryman.

relations.name: Odile Vance
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She sets the quarrymen's bones and says the cutting was wrong. I do not want a healer's sermons, but she is good at what she does.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: works cook
relations.note: She feeds the works and wants her husband off the road. A sensible woman with a sensible worry.

relations.name: Tobiah Marsh
relations.label: crate-maker
relations.note: He makes the crates for Silas's loads and grumbles at the Brackenford due. A careful man with a saw, and I pay him for it.

relations.name: Wenna Marrow
relations.label: the weaver's daughter
relations.note: She is the reason my daughter was shamed. I have nothing to say to her and less to say of her.

memories.gist: Tobin Marrow broke his promise to Hester a month before the wedding; I stood in the Council yard and heard the town talk.
The quarrymen cut into a giants' cairn on the ridge, and Hollbrenna closed the shelf to us; I will not beg her pardon.
I promised Lanternquay a great quantity of seawall stone at Hester's price, and the works cannot cut it fast enough.
Pell ran from the foundry before his indenture ended; I offered marks for word of him.
Silas Pike was robbed twice on the stone road and still brought the load through; I remember that.

stances.why: A contract is a man's word, and mine is the works.
Hollbrenna closed the shelf; I will not go to her on my knees.
He ran from his indenture, and if one boy runs the rest will follow.
Brackenford's due robs every carter and drives trade away.
Aldric's son insulted my house, and Kettlebridge remembers.

pastimes: Walking the foundry floor at first light, feeling the heat off the iron
Playing cards at the works' back table with masters and carters
Climbing to the ridge to look down at the works and the town he built
Josiah Crane.calling: I built this works with my hands and my word, and every load that leaves my gate carries my name on it.

Prudence Crane.narrative: I keep the foundry house and its table, and the Council's masters eat here after every sitting. I hear what they say and I keep it. The Marrows owe my house an apology, and I have not had it; until I do, they will not sit at my table.
goals: Keep the foundry house and its table as it should be
See the Marrows apologise for the broken match
Keep the Council's masters fed and their talk in the house
See the foundry house pass to Hester in good order, with a table she is proud of
Hear the Marrows' apology spoken aloud, in her own house, before she dies
Prudence Crane.mood: warm to her own, cold to the Marrows

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He built this works with his hands, and I keep his house and his table.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She keeps the books and her own counsel; I am proud of her.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: grudge
relations.note: His son insulted my house, and he has never come to apologise.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: betrayer
relations.note: He broke his promise to my daughter and shamed us before both towns.

relations.name: Ambrose Vell
relations.label: council master
relations.note: He eats at my table and speaks slowly; I keep his plate warm.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: clerk
relations.note: He winds the clock and writes the contracts; he is careful at my table.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: workman
relations.note: He works cheap for my husband; I have no quarrel with him.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He builds the crates and grumbles about the cheap hands; I feed him all the same.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: She has not paid for the stone, and I hear it at my table.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: works cook
relations.note: She feeds the works and I feed the masters. We understand each other's work.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: She keeps an ironware stall in the square and trades with our foundry. She is sharp and I like her.

memories.gist: Tobin Marrow broke his promise to Hester a month before the wedding; I set the table that night for a house that had been shamed.
I fed the Council's masters after the sitting where they argued the gate-due and the stone price.
Hester told me she was glad the match broke; I have kept that to myself.
I heard at my own table that Lanternquay had not paid for the last load.

stances.why: The Council eats here, and a house is judged by its table.
The Marrows shamed my house and have never come to say sorry.
A fed master speaks freely, and I hear what is said.
Hester and Josiah are my house, and I will not see them shamed again.

pastimes: Tending the foundry house garden and its herbs for the table
Baking the bread and pies for Council sittings, and hearing every word over them
Visiting the poor terrace with a basket, and knowing every family there by name
Prudence Crane.calling: I keep the foundry house and its table, and a house kept well is a work as good as any iron that leaves the yard.

Ambrose Vell.narrative: I am old master of the brickworks and second voice on the Works Council. I speak slowly and forgive more slowly. Josiah is my chair and my friend, but I think the tithe should be forgiven this winter, though I will not fight him over a farmer. The gate-due at Brackenford is a robbery, and I have said so.
goals: Keep the brickworks and the kiln yard in good order
See the gate-due at Brackenford dropped
Hold the Council together behind Josiah
Fire a batch of bricks as true as any he made in his prime, one more time
See the gate-due at Brackenford dropped in his lifetime

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: council chair
relations.note: He chairs the Council and I sit second; he is a hard man but a straight one.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: clerk
relations.note: She keeps the foundry books and knows them; I respect that.

relations.name: Prudence Crane
relations.label: hostess
relations.note: She feeds the Council after every sitting, and I am glad of it.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: clerk
relations.note: He writes the contracts and winds the clock; a careful man.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He rents my kiln yard and led the cutting; I keep my peace with him.

relations.name: Hedley Ashcombe
relations.label: farmer
relations.note: He is behind on his tithe, and I think it should be forgiven this winter.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He builds the seawall crates; he owes Josiah for brick and I hear of it.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He has been robbed twice and still carries; a good man on the road.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He keeps the gate-due that robs every carter, and I have no love for it.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: works hand
relations.note: He came up from the quay and works cheap. The builders resent him, but the man has to eat.

relations.name: Silas Vance
relations.label: quarry foreman
relations.note: He worked the cutting beside Ezra and has not gone back up the ridge since. A foreman who will not go where he sends his men is no foreman; still, he has not lied about it, and I am slow to condemn a man for fear.

relations.name: Verity Ashcombe
relations.label: farmer's wife
relations.note: She knows which strips will fail and keeps the seed store against it. If the Council had her sense, we would count Hedley's greens and be done. I will not fight Josiah over a farmer, but she is the one I would listen to.

memories.gist: I sat second on the Council when Josiah sent stone south to Lanternquay as much as north to Brackenford.
The quarrymen cut into a giants' cairn on the ridge; I said little, but I remember the silence in the Council yard.
I argued at the sitting that Hedley Ashcombe's tithe should be forgiven this winter, and Josiah would not hear it.
I buried an old foundry hand who had worked beside me; the Crane men carried him.

stances.why: The winter is hard and the store is short; a farmer cannot pay in grain he does not have.
Brackenford's due robs every carter and sours the road.
The works stand on the Council, and the Council stands on Josiah.
The brickworks and the kiln yard are my life's work.

pastimes: Sitting on the kiln-yard wall at evening, watching the bricks cool
Fishing the river below the terraces with a long rod and no hurry
Telling the young apprentices how the brickworks was when he was a lad
Ambrose Vell.calling: The brickworks is my life's work, and a good brick laid true will outlast every quarrel on this island.
